questions.question: Who succeeded M. Venkaiah Naidu as the Vice President of India in 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagdeep Dhankhar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagdeep Dhankhar** succeeded **M. Venkaiah Naidu** as the **Vice President of India** on **August 11, 2022**, following the completion of Naidu's term.
 
• He was elected as the **14th Vice President of India** and is also the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**, as per the constitutional provision of the Vice President's role.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankhar is a seasoned politician and lawyer, having previously served as the **Governor of West Bengal** from **July 2019 to July 2022**.
 
• The election for the Vice President was held on **August 6, 2022**, and Dhankhar emerged victorious by securing a significant majority of votes, defeating the opposition candidate **Margaret Alva**.
 
• The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the **Members of Parliament (MPs) from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha**. This election is conducted by secret ballot, following the system of proportional representation by a single transferable vote.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankhar's leadership and extensive experience in politics, law, and governance played a crucial role in his selection for this esteemed position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jagdeep Dhankhar:**

 
 
• **Born:** May 18, 1951, in **Kithana, Rajasthan**, Jagdeep Dhankhar is known for his distinguished career in both politics and law.
 
• He served as a Member of Parliament (MP) from **Jhunjhunu constituency** in Rajasthan during 1989-1991 and has been associated with the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**.
 
• He has also served as the Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs in the **Chandra Shekhar government** (1990-1991).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Vice President of India:**
 
 
• The Vice President is the **second-highest constitutional office** in India after the President. The primary responsibility is to act as the **Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• In the event of the President's absence, resignation, or removal, the Vice President may act as the **President of India** temporarily.
 
 
 
• **M. Venkaiah Naidu:**
 
 
• **M. Venkaiah Naidu** served as the **13th Vice President of India** from **August 11, 2017, to August 10, 2022**.
 
• He is a prominent leader from the BJP and is well-known for his contributions to policy-making and governance during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **Other Candidates for Vice President in 2022:**
 
 
• **Margaret Alva**, the opposition candidate, contested against Dhankhar but lost the election with a significant margin.
 
• The election showcased the importance of strong political alliances, as Dhankhar secured the backing of the **NDA (National Democratic Alliance)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Election Process:**

 
 
• The Vice President is elected through an electoral college comprising **Members of Parliament** (MPs) from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• The election is conducted using a **single transferable vote** system through a secret ballot.
 
 
 
• **Vice President's Tenure:**
 
 
• The Vice President serves a term of **five years** but can be re-elected for subsequent terms.
 
• In case of resignation or removal, the Vice President can vacate the office before completing the term.

questions.question: In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which of the following provisions has been introduced for the first time concerning crimes against women?

options.text: Inclusion of community service as a punishment for domestic violence.
Provision for capital punishment in cases of gang rape of a woman under 18 years.
Reduction of the age of consent for sexual activities to 16 years.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Provision for capital punishment in cases of gang rape of a woman under 18 years.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, is a proposed replacement for the Indian Penal Code (IPC). It introduces several new provisions aimed at modernizing India's criminal justice system.
 
• One of the key provisions introduced in the **BNS, 2023**, is the **provision for capital punishment** in cases of the **gang rape of a woman under the age of 18 years**, which was not explicitly included in the earlier IPC framework. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The inclusion of this provision reflects a stronger stance towards crimes against women, particularly minors, ensuring stricter penalties for heinous crimes.
 
• Other options like community service for domestic violence, legalization of marital rape, or lowering the age of consent to 16 years are not part of the provisions in **BNS, 2023**. Hence, these statements are incorrect.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Provisions Related to Crimes Against Women in BNS, 2023:**

 
 
• **Capital Punishment:** The introduction of capital punishment in cases of gang rape of a woman under 18 years reflects the government’s commitment to addressing sexual violence with the highest degree of seriousness.
 
• **Focus on Women’s Safety:** The **BNS, 2023**, emphasizes stricter laws for crimes against women to deter offenders and ensure faster delivery of justice.
 
 
 
• **Details of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Inclusion of community service as a punishment for domestic violence:** No such provision has been included in the **BNS, 2023**. Domestic violence laws in India are primarily governed by the **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**, which focuses on protective orders rather than community service.
 
• **Legalization of marital rape:** Marital rape is not legalized under **BNS, 2023**. The debate around criminalizing marital rape continues, and it remains a complex socio-legal issue in India.
 
• **Reduction of the age of consent for sexual activities to 16 years:** The age of consent in India remains **18 years** under the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012**. The **BNS, 2023**, does not propose any changes to this.
 
 
 
• **Background of BNS, 2023:**
 
 
• The **BNS, 2023**, was introduced to replace colonial-era laws like the **Indian Penal Code (1860)**, aiming to modernize the criminal justice system in alignment with contemporary needs.
 
• It seeks to address gaps in the existing legal framework, particularly concerning crimes against women, children, and vulnerable groups.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of BNS, 2023:**

 
 
• The **BNS, 2023**, introduces provisions for faster trials and stricter punishments for specific crimes, including sexual offenses.
 
• It aims to decolonize the Indian legal system by replacing laws introduced during British rule, focusing on a more victim-centric approach.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Capital Punishment Provision:**
 
 
• The inclusion of capital punishment for gang rape cases involving minors under 18 years serves as a strong deterrent against such heinous crimes.
 
• It aligns with public demand for stricter laws to safeguard women and children, particularly in light of high-profile cases of sexual violence in India.
 
 
 
• **Legal and Social Implications:**
 
 
• The **BNS, 2023**, aims to balance retributive justice with preventive measures, ensuring better protection for vulnerable groups.
 
• The provision also reflects India’s commitment to international conventions on women’s and children’s rights, such as the **Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW)**.

• **The first Commonwealth Games** were held in **1930** in the city of **Hamilton, Canada.** This marked the beginning of an international sporting competition among the member nations of the British Empire.
 
• The games were initially called the **British Empire Games,** and they aimed to promote goodwill and friendly rivalry among the Commonwealth countries.
 
• A total of **11 countries** participated in the first edition of the games, featuring **400 athletes** competing in six sports and 59 events. *Hence, the correct answer is Canada.*

• **Historical Context of the Commonwealth Games:**

 
 
• The **Commonwealth Games** originated as the **British Empire Games** in 1930, reflecting the unity and cooperation among countries in the British Empire.
 
• The name was later changed to the **British Empire and Commonwealth Games** in 1954, and then to the **British Commonwealth Games** in 1970, before finally being called the Commonwealth Games in 1978.
 
 
 
• **Features of the First Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• The first edition of the games included **six sports:** athletics, swimming, rowing, boxing, wrestling, and lawn bowls.
 
• **Participants:** The games witnessed participation from 11 countries, including **Canada, Australia, England, South Africa, and New Zealand.**
 
• **Hamilton's Contribution:** The city of **Hamilton, Ontario,** funded and supported the games, showcasing its commitment to international sports.

• Over the years, the games have grown to include over **70 member countries** and territories, competing in a wide range of sports.
 
• The Commonwealth Games is unique because it includes sports that are often popular in Commonwealth nations, such as **netball, rugby sevens, and lawn bowls.**
 
• The games also emphasize **equality** by featuring events for athletes with disabilities in the same program as able-bodied athletes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Developments in Commonwealth Games History:**

 
 
• **1954:** The games in Vancouver introduced the **Queen's Baton Relay,** a tradition that continues to this day, symbolizing the unity of the Commonwealth.
 
• **1998:** Kuala Lumpur games were the first to include **team sports** like cricket and hockey.
 
• **2010:** The Commonwealth Games were held in **India** for the first time, in New Delhi, featuring an extensive program of sports and cultural events.

• They also showcase the **cultural diversity** and sporting talents of the Commonwealth nations.

questions.question: What is the primary reason for tides on Earth?

options.text: Gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tides are caused by gravitational forces:** The primary reason for tides on Earth is the **gravitational pull exerted by the Moon and the Sun**. The Moon's gravitational pull has a stronger influence due to its proximity to Earth.
 
• The gravitational force of the Moon creates a bulge in the oceans on the side facing the Moon, known as the **direct tide**. Simultaneously, another bulge occurs on the opposite side due to inertia, forming the **opposite tide**.
 
• The Sun, though farther away, also contributes to tides. Its gravitational pull interacts with the Moon's pull, creating **spring tides** (strongest tides) and **neap tides** (weakest tides) depending on their alignment.
 
• **High tides and low tides:** Tides result in alternating high and low water levels, which occur twice daily. These fluctuations depend on the rotation of Earth and the relative positions of the Moon and Sun.
 
• The gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun works in tandem with Earth's rotation to create **cyclical tidal patterns**. This is crucial for understanding the movement of water bodies.
 
• Hence, the statement that tides are primarily caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun is *correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Tides:**

 
 
• **Spring Tides:** These occur when the Earth, Moon, and Sun are in alignment during the full moon and new moon phases. The combined gravitational forces result in higher high tides and lower low tides.
 
• **Neap Tides:** These occur when the Moon and Sun are at right angles to each other during the first and third quarter phases of the Moon. The gravitational forces partly cancel each other out, resulting in weaker tides.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Moon:**
 
 
• The Moon's proximity to Earth makes its gravitational influence the dominant factor in the formation of tides. It creates a tidal bulge on the side closest to the Moon.
 
• The opposite side of Earth also experiences a tidal bulge due to centrifugal forces resulting from Earth's rotation.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Sun:**
 
 
• The Sun's gravitational pull is weaker than the Moon's because it is much farther from Earth. However, it still plays a significant role in amplifying or diminishing tides depending on its alignment with the Moon.
 
• When the Sun and Moon align, their combined gravitational forces create spring tides. Conversely, during perpendicular alignment, neap tides are formed.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**
 
 
• Tides affect coastal ecosystems, navigation, and fishing industries. They also play a role in maintaining the balance of marine environments.
 
• The study of tides is essential for understanding Earth's gravitational interactions with celestial bodies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tidal Energy:**

 
 
• **Tidal energy** is harnessed from tidal movements and is considered a renewable energy source. This energy is generated using tidal turbines or barrages.
 
• Examples of tidal energy projects include the **La Rance tidal power station in France**, one of the earliest tidal power plants.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Studies:**
 
 
• The study of tides contributes to understanding Earth's **gravitational interactions** with the Moon and Sun, as well as the effects of Earth's rotation.
 
• Tidal patterns are critical for predicting **natural phenomena** such as tsunamis and coastal flooding.

questions.question: Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of the constituent assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** was appointed as the **Chairman of the Drafting Committee** of the **Constituent Assembly of India**, which was tasked with drafting the Constitution of India.
 
• The Drafting Committee, chaired by **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**, consisted of seven members, including notable leaders like **Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer**, **K. M. Munshi**, and **Gopalaswami Ayyangar**.
 
• **Dr. Ambedkar** played a pivotal role in shaping the Indian Constitution and is often referred to as the "**Father of the Indian Constitution**" due to his significant contributions.
 
• The Drafting Committee was formed on **29th August 1947**, and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was unanimously chosen as its Chairman owing to his expertise in law, economics, and social reforms.
 
• The Indian Constitution, drafted under the guidance of **Dr. Ambedkar**, was adopted on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.***

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of the Drafting Committee:**

 
 
• The Drafting Committee was responsible for preparing the **draft Constitution of India**. It worked on incorporating various principles and provisions to ensure justice, equality, liberty, and fraternity for all citizens.
 
• The committee deliberated on issues such as **fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, federal structure**, and the separation of powers.
 
 
 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's Contributions:**
 
 
• **Dr. Ambedkar** was a renowned social reformer, jurist, and economist. His vision shaped the Constitution to address issues of **social inequality and discrimination**.
 
• He advocated for provisions to eliminate caste-based discrimination and ensure equal opportunities for all, including the **reservation system** for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
• He emphasized the importance of **individual rights, secularism, and social justice**, which became the cornerstone of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Other Members of the Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• **Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer:** A legal luminary who contributed to framing the federal structure.
 
• **K. M. Munshi:** Played a significant role in drafting the preamble and ensuring linguistic and cultural preservation.
 
• **Gopalaswami Ayyangar:** Contributed to discussions on state reorganization and the federal system.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Formation of Constituent Assembly:**

 
 
• The **Constituent Assembly of India** was formed in **1946** under the Cabinet Mission Plan. It consisted of members elected by provincial assemblies and nominated by princely states.
 
• The Assembly had **299 members**, representing diverse regions, communities, and interests.
 
 
 
• **Adoption of the Constitution:**
 
 
• The Constitution was adopted on **26th November 1949** and enforced on **26th January 1950**, marking the beginning of India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.
 
• The date **26th January** was chosen to commemorate the **Purna Swaraj Declaration of 1930**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an indirect tax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Tax:** An indirect tax is a tax imposed on goods and services rather than on income or profits. Consumers pay this tax indirectly as part of the purchase price of goods or services.
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST):** GST is a comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services across India. It is a multi-stage, destination-based tax system aimed at eliminating cascading taxes.
 
• GST is categorized as an indirect tax because it is collected by businesses from consumers at the point of sale and remitted to the government. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• Income Tax (Option 1): It is a direct tax levied on an individual's or entity's income by the government. *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
• Corporate Tax (Option 2): This is a direct tax imposed on the net income or profit of companies. *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
• Wealth Tax (Option 4): This is a direct tax levied on the net wealth of an individual, entity, or Hindu Undivided Family (HUF). *Hence, this is not correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Indirect Taxes:**

 
 
• Indirect taxes are levied on the consumption of goods and services and are ultimately paid by the end consumer.
 
• The seller or service provider collects the tax from consumers and remits it to the government.
 
• Examples of indirect taxes include **GST, customs duty, excise duty, and value-added tax (VAT).**
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of GST:**
 
 
• GST was introduced in **India on 1st July 2017** under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• It is classified into **Central GST (CGST)** and **State GST (SGST)** for intra-state transactions and **Integrated GST (IGST)** for inter-state transactions.
 
• GST replaced multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, VAT, and customs duty, streamlining the taxation system in India.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of GST:**
 
 
• Eliminates cascading taxes and reduces the overall tax burden on consumers.
 
• Promotes ease of doing business by providing a unified taxation system.
 
• Encourages transparency in tax collection and compliance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Understanding Direct Taxes vs. Indirect Taxes:**

 
 
• **Direct Taxes:** Levied directly on an individual's or entity's income, wealth, or profit. Examples include **income tax, corporate tax, and wealth tax.**
 
• **Indirect Taxes:** Applied to goods and services, and the burden is passed on to the end consumer. Examples include **GST, customs duty, and excise duty.**
 
 
 
• **Global Adoption of GST:**
 
 
• Over **160 countries** globally have implemented GST or similar value-added taxes, including **Canada, Australia, and European Union nations.**
 
• It is recognized as an efficient taxation model to promote economic growth and reduce tax evasion.

questions.question: Which Indian biosphere reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve** is a unique natural ecosystem located in the eastern part of India, predominantly in the state of **West Bengal**.
 
• It is part of the **Sundarbans Delta**, which is the largest delta in the world formed by the confluence of the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers**.
 
• The Sundarbans is known for its extensive mangrove forests, which are among the largest in the world and act as a natural barrier against cyclones and coastal erosion. *Hence, the Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.*
 
• **UNESCO designated the Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve as a World Heritage Site** in **1987**, recognizing its ecological significance and the role it plays in supporting biodiversity.
 
• It is home to the **Royal Bengal Tiger**, along with other species such as estuarine crocodiles, Indian python, and spotted deer. The mangroves also serve as a breeding ground for diverse fish species and aquatic life. *Hence, it is globally significant for biodiversity conservation.*
 
• The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve plays a crucial role in regulating the climatic conditions of the region and mitigating the effects of **climate change** and rising sea levels.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Other Biosphere Reserves:**

 
 
• **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve:** Located in the Western Ghats and spans parts of **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka**. It is known for its rich biodiversity and houses **rare species like the Nilgiri Tahr and Lion-tailed Macaque.**
 
• **Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve:** Situated in the state of **Uttarakhand**. It is recognized for its **snow-clad peaks, alpine meadows, and the Nanda Devi National Park**, which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve:** Located along the southeastern coast of Tamil Nadu. It is known for its **marine biodiversity** and coral reefs, including more than **4,000 species of flora and fauna.**
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• It is globally significant for its **mangroves**, which contribute to reducing the impact of cyclones, coastal flooding, and erosion.
 
• Its biodiversity includes **300 species of birds**, **aquatic life**, and endangered species like the **Royal Bengal Tiger.**
 
• The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve also supports the livelihoods of local communities through **fishing and honey collection.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**

 
 
• UNESCO recognizes **natural and cultural sites** of outstanding universal value. The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve was designated as a World Heritage Site in **1987**.
 
• It highlights the importance of mangrove ecosystems in supporting biodiversity and mitigating climate change impacts.
 
 
 
• **Biosphere Reserves in India:**
 
 
• India has a total of **18 Biosphere Reserves**, out of which **11** are part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
• They play a significant role in **conservation, research, and sustainable development** of ecosystems and communities.
 
• Examples include **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** and **Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve**, which are also recognized globally.

questions.question: What does the term 'crowding out' refer to in economics?

options.text: Decline in private investment due to high government borrowing
Rise in inflation due to excessive printing of money

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decline in private investment due to high government borrowing.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Crowding Out:** In economics, **crowding out** refers to a situation where increased **government borrowing or expenditure** leads to a **reduction in private sector investment**. This occurs because government borrowing increases the demand for funds in the financial market, driving up interest rates.
 
• **Mechanism:** When a government borrows heavily to finance its deficit, it competes with private borrowers for available funds in the market. This competition raises the **cost of borrowing (interest rates)**, making it less attractive for private businesses to take loans for investment. This phenomenon is known as the **crowding-out effect.**
 
• **Impact on Private Investment:** Higher interest rates discourage private sector firms from investing in new projects, as the cost of financing increases. This can lead to a **decline in economic growth** in the long run due to reduced private sector expansion.
 
• **Example:** If a government issues a large volume of bonds to fund infrastructure projects, banks and financial institutions may prefer to invest in these bonds because they are safer and offer competitive returns. This reduces the funds available for loans to businesses, which is a classic example of crowding out.
 
• **Implications:** While government spending can stimulate the economy in the short term, excessive borrowing can lead to unintended consequences like reduced private investment, slower economic growth, and even inflationary pressures.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Impacts of Crowding Out:**

 
 
• **Reduced Private Sector Growth:** The private sector plays a crucial role in generating employment and driving innovation. Crowding out hampers private growth by reducing access to credit.
 
• **Economic Imbalance:** Over-reliance on government spending can lead to an unbalanced economy, where private sector activities are suppressed.
 
 
 
• **Relation to Fiscal Policy:**
 
 
• Crowding out is often associated with **expansionary fiscal policy**, where governments increase spending to boost economic activity. However, excessive spending can result in negative outcomes like reduced private sector participation.
 
• **Keynesian vs. Classical Views:** Keynesian economists argue that government spending is necessary to stimulate demand during economic downturns, while classical economists caution against crowding out, as it may harm long-term economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples:**
 
 
• **United States:** During periods of high government borrowing, such as World War II and the 2008 financial crisis, private investment temporarily declined due to the crowding-out effect.
 
• **India:** In times of fiscal deficit, the Indian government’s heavy borrowing has occasionally led to higher interest rates, impacting private investment.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Option 2:** "Increase in competition among businesses" refers to market dynamics where businesses compete for market share. It is unrelated to the concept of crowding out.
 
• **Option 3:** "Reduction in export demand" pertains to external trade and is typically influenced by factors like exchange rates, global demand, and tariffs, not government borrowing.
 
• **Option 4:** "Rise in inflation due to excessive printing of money" relates to monetary policy, where excessive currency supply devalues money, causing inflation. This is distinct from crowding out caused by borrowing.
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:** Crowding out is a critical concept in economics that highlights the potential trade-offs between government spending and private sector investment, emphasizing the need for balanced fiscal management.

questions.question: The origin of the Ganga River is from which of the following?

• The **Ganga River** originates from the **Gangotri Glacier**, which is located in the **Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand**, India.
 
• The river emerges in the form of the **Bhagirathi River** from **Gaumukh**, a cave-like structure at the snout of the glacier.
 
• The **Bhagirathi** later converges with the **Alaknanda River** at **Devprayag**, marking the official beginning of the Ganga River.
 
• The **Gangotri Glacier** is around **30.2 kilometers long** and **2 to 4 kilometers wide**, making it one of the largest glaciers in the Himalayas.
 
• The glacier is situated at an altitude of approximately **7,100 meters above sea level**, surrounded by peaks like **Chaukhamba, Shivling, and Bhagirathi**.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Gangotri Glacier.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gangotri Glacier:**

 
 
• The glacier is a primary source of water for the Ganga River, which is considered sacred in Hinduism.
 
• It is a retreating glacier, with its snout (Gaumukh) receding approximately 10 to 30 meters annually due to **climate change** and global warming.

• **Siachen Glacier:** Located in the eastern Karakoram range in Ladakh, it is the largest glacier in the Indian subcontinent but does not contribute to the Ganga River.
 
• **Zemu Glacier:** Found in Sikkim, this glacier feeds the Teesta River, which flows through Sikkim and West Bengal.
 
• **Pindari Glacier:** Located in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, it forms the Pindar River, a tributary of the Alaknanda River.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Ganga River:**

• **Religious Significance:**
 
 
• The Ganga is believed to cleanse sins and is a major site for **ritual bathing** and cremation along its ghats.
 
• Prominent pilgrimage sites along the river include **Haridwar, Varanasi, and Prayagraj**.

• The TPP underwent revisions in subsequent years, such as in **1982, 1986, and 2006**, to align it with changing socio-economic priorities and challenges. These revisions expanded its scope and made it more effective in addressing rural poverty.
 
• The program included measures for **land reforms, welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and an increase in literacy rates**. It also emphasized **family planning, environmental protection, and the development of rural infrastructure**.
 
• The program played a crucial role in bringing attention to **inclusive growth** and ensuring that economic development reached the grassroots level, particularly in rural areas.
 
• *Hence, the Twenty Point Program was a significant initiative to address rural poverty in India.*

__
 
• **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP):**

• Though it contributed to improving living conditions, it was not directly focused on eradicating rural poverty in the same comprehensive way as the Twenty Point Program.
 
 
 
• **Employment Guarantee Scheme (EGS):**
 
 
• This was a state-level initiative introduced in **Maharashtra in 1972** to provide **employment opportunities to rural laborers** during periods of drought or unemployment.
 
• It laid the foundation for national programs like the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, but its scope was more localized compared to the Twenty Point Program.

• **Objectives of the Twenty Point Program:**

questions.question: Which plant part carries out the process of photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leaf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis:** The process by which **green plants** and certain other organisms convert **light energy** into chemical energy stored in the form of glucose. The reaction primarily occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells.
 
• Leaves are the primary site for photosynthesis because they contain a high concentration of **chlorophyll**, a pigment that absorbs light energy.
 
• Leaves possess specialized structures such as **stomata** (tiny openings) that facilitate gas exchange, allowing **carbon dioxide** to enter and **oxygen** to exit. Hence, the leaf is the correct part for photosynthesis.
 
• Other plant parts like the **stem, root, and flower** do not contain significant amounts of chlorophyll and are not involved in photosynthesis. Their roles are limited to support, nutrient absorption, and reproduction, respectively. Hence, these options are incorrect.
 
• The **mesophyll cells** in the leaf contain chloroplasts where the light-dependent and light-independent reactions of photosynthesis occur, leading to the production of glucose and oxygen.
 
• The leaf's structure, including its large surface area and thinness, maximizes light absorption and efficient gas exchange, making it the most suitable organ for photosynthesis.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Leaf.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis Process:**

 
 
• **Light-dependent reactions:** Occur in the **thylakoid membranes** of chloroplasts where light energy is converted into chemical energy (ATP and NADPH).
 
• **Calvin Cycle:** Occurs in the chloroplast’s **stroma**, where ATP and NADPH are used to convert **carbon dioxide** into glucose.
 
 
 
• **Features of Leaves:**
 
 
• Leaves are flat and broad, maximizing their exposure to sunlight.
 
• They contain numerous **chloroplasts** with chlorophyll for absorbing sunlight.
 
• The presence of **veins** in leaves helps transport water and nutrients and remove glucose.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Plant Parts:**
 
 
• **Roots:** Responsible for absorbing water and minerals from the soil, but do not perform photosynthesis.
 
• **Stem:** Provides structural support and transports water, nutrients, and sugars between roots and leaves.
 
• **Flowers:** Involved in reproduction and do not have chlorophyll for photosynthesis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Photosynthesis Equation:**

 
 
• **6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂**. This equation represents the process where **carbon dioxide** and **water** are converted into glucose and oxygen using sunlight.
 
• This process is vital for maintaining the earth’s oxygen levels and serves as the primary energy source for all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chlorophyll:**
 
 
• Chlorophyll absorbs **blue and red light** from the sun and reflects green light, giving leaves their characteristic green color.
 
• It is essential for capturing sunlight and enabling the conversion of energy into chemical bonds.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Photosynthetic Plants:**
 
 
• All green plants like **mango, wheat, and rice** perform photosynthesis using their leaves.
 
• Certain algae and cyanobacteria also perform photosynthesis using similar processes.

questions.question: Which device is commonly used to measure temperature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermometer:** A thermometer is a scientific instrument used to measure temperature. It provides readings in units such as Celsius, Fahrenheit, or Kelvin.
 
• Thermometers work based on the principle of thermal expansion or the change in physical properties of materials (e.g., mercury or alcohol) when heated or cooled.
 
• They are widely used in various fields, including **medical, industrial, meteorological, and research applications**. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Barometer:** This device measures atmospheric pressure and is not designed to measure temperature. It is primarily used in meteorology. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Speedometer:** A speedometer measures the speed of a vehicle. It has no relation to temperature measurement. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Altimeter:** An altimeter measures altitude or the height above sea level. It is used in aviation and mountaineering, not for temperature measurement. *Hence, this is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermometer Types:**

 
 
• **Mercury Thermometers:** These thermometers use mercury in a glass tube. They are highly accurate and used in laboratories and medical settings.
 
• **Digital Thermometers:** These devices provide temperature readings in a digital format and are commonly used in homes and hospitals due to their ease of use.
 
• **Infrared Thermometers:** These thermometers measure temperature from a distance by detecting infrared radiation emitted by an object. They are widely used in industrial and medical fields.
 
• **Alcohol Thermometers:** These use alcohol dyed for visibility and are suitable for measuring lower temperatures, as alcohol has a lower freezing point than mercury.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Thermometers:**
 
 
• **Medical Use:** Thermometers are essential in healthcare to monitor body temperature and diagnose fever or hypothermia.
 
• **Weather Monitoring:** Meteorologists use thermometers to measure ambient air temperature for weather forecasts.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Thermometers are crucial in industries such as manufacturing, food processing, and chemical production to ensure proper temperature control.
 
• **Scientific Research:** Precise temperature measurement is essential in experiments related to physics, chemistry, and biology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History of Thermometers:**

 
 
• **Gabriel Fahrenheit:** Invented the mercury thermometer in **1714**, introducing the Fahrenheit scale.
 
• **Anders Celsius:** Developed the Celsius scale in **1742**, widely used in scientific and daily temperature measurements.
 
 
 
• **Key Scientific Principles:**
 
 
• **Thermal Expansion:** Materials expand or contract with temperature changes, a principle used in traditional thermometers.
 
• **Infrared Radiation:** Infrared thermometers detect heat radiation, enabling non-contact temperature measurement.
 
 
 
• **Global Standards:**
 
 
• Temperature measurements follow internationally recognized units like **Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin**, standardized for consistency.

questions.question: Lohri, a popular festival of North India, is mainly associated with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Sugarcane harvesting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lohri** is a vibrant festival celebrated mainly in **Punjab** and parts of **North India**. It is observed on **13th January** every year.
 
• The festival marks the end of the **winter solstice** and is a celebration of the harvest season.
 
• **Sugarcane harvesting** plays a central role in Lohri celebrations. Farmers celebrate the successful harvest of sugarcane, which is one of the primary crops in Punjab and Haryana. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• During Lohri, people light a bonfire and offer items like **jaggery**, **rewari**, **popcorn**, and **sesame seeds** to the fire as part of the rituals, symbolizing gratitude for the harvest.
 
• Although Lohri is associated with the harvest season, it is specifically tied to the harvesting of sugarcane rather than rice or mangoes. *Hence, option 1 and option 4 are incorrect.*
 
• The festival is also associated with the **winter solstice**, as it marks the transition to longer days. However, the primary focus is on sugarcane harvesting. *Hence, option 2 is partially correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 3) Sugarcane harvesting.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lohri Festival:**

 
 
• Lohri is considered a festival of farmers and is celebrated with great enthusiasm in **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and parts of **Delhi**.
 
• It is a harvest festival that is celebrated after the sowing of the **rabi crops**. Farmers thank **God** for the bountiful harvest.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Sugarcane:**
 
 
• **Sugarcane** is one of the most important crops in Punjab and Haryana. Its harvest marks the beginning of Lohri celebrations.
 
• Sugarcane is used to make **jaggery**, which is a key offering during the rituals of the festival.
 
• Products like **rewari** and **gachak**, prepared using sugarcane and sesame, are distributed among family and friends during Lohri.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Elements:**
 
 
• Traditional songs and dances such as **bhangra** and **gidda** are performed around the bonfire.
 
• The festival is also an occasion for family gatherings and sharing joy.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:**
 
 
• Lohri is predominantly celebrated in **Punjab** and northern regions of **India**, where sugarcane is a major crop.
 
• The festival reflects the agrarian lifestyle and traditions of these areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Festivals Related to Harvest:**

 
 
• **Pongal:** Celebrated in **Tamil Nadu**, it marks the harvest of rice and other crops.
 
• **Makar Sankranti:** Observed across India, it signifies the sun's transition into the zodiac sign of Capricorn and is associated with harvest celebrations.
 
• **Bihu:** Celebrated in **Assam**, it marks the harvesting of paddy.
 
 
 
• **Historical and Social Significance:**
 
 
• Lohri is an occasion to celebrate unity, express gratitude to nature, and share prosperity among the community.
 
• The festival has evolved as a cultural symbol of **joy** and **togetherness** in North India.
